reference.title: Example Reference Topic
reference.shortdesc: A DITA topic of type reference. This is a shared topic.

change-item.change-summary: This is a shared topic. If you change it, you change it for everyone. This is a part of the change-historylist which is part of the metadata of the topic. It is not included in the output. It allows for file history to be stored in the file. You can use this manually as a way to log changes, or you could write scripts that automagically populate this information.

section.p: You cannot just work in the refbody, you have to add child element first. This is a section (without a title). If I want a reference topic with just text (or a definition list) in it, I use a section.
A reference topic allows the following elements in the refbody:

ul.li: example — A specialized section that can contain any of the basic authoring elements that's intended to be an example of something.
properties — A specialized table for a list of properties and description. (This option is going away and is rarely used. I would avoid using it.)
refsyn — A specialized section container for syntax items. Syntax generally refers to command line or programming objects. This block can contain any of the basic authoring elements.
section — A container for any of the basic authoring elements.
table — A table. If you feel you need some introductory text, you'll have to add a section element before the table.

example.title: Example with a title
example.p: Similar to using an example in a concept topic, the example is for a blob of text or whatever, but the intention is that it is an example of something.

property.propvalue: Another property value for the same proptype

refsyn.title: refsyn
refsyn.p: Again, the refsyn is just like a section, but it contains the semantic meaning of syntax reference for programming languages or command line tools.
